findings.region: Both large felt surfaces across the middle of the full room; left roughlyx180..495/y345..486, rightx624..1010/y340..488.
findings.observation: The candidate turns the original green wall panels into large steeply sloped felt quadrilaterals, but almost all visible furniture height is still occupied by the felt surface. The apron and short narrow supports form a shallow strip beneath it. In the full room the objects read as tilted panels or low platforms rather than full-height freestanding gaming tables.
findings.comparison: Original upright panels are visibly wrong as tables. Adding visible pegs in the candidate improves the silhouette without resolving the whole-room physical reading.

findings.region: The feet and wall/floor seam aroundscreeny470..487.
findings.observation: The feet terminate immediately beside the back wall/floor seam. There is little readable floor extending behind and under the furniture, and no distinct contact-shadow footprint separates each table body from the wall. This reinforces wall attachment even where supports can be counted.

findings.region: Private Table/Vic Mercer and the two high-stakes guards in front of the right felt plane.
findings.observation: The unchanged populated actors provide the scale reference: the large rear surface rises behind them like a slanted board, while the table underbody is compressed behind their lower silhouettes. Their presence makes the plane/body imbalance clearer than an isolated empty-table image.

uncertainties: The exact body/label occlusion constraints are technically recorded, but a count of contact-clear pixels cannot determine a believable furniture height or room perspective.
